content.user_title: Write Clearer Prompts With Proven Standards
content.value_statement: Vague, bloated prompts waste tokens and produce unreliable AI output. This skill applies context engineering standards that keep prompts clear, structured, and focused on high-signal information.
actual_capabilities: Guides you to structure prompts with clear Markdown sections for background, instructions, examples, and constraints.
Rewrites verbose or indirect language into direct, imperative instructions.
Applies just-in-time context loading so prompts reference data instead of dumping it inline.
Provides a review checklist to confirm clarity, structure, and minimal redundancy.
Offers step-by-step workflows for both creating a new prompt and optimizing an existing one.
Explains context engineering principles drawn from published Anthropic guidance.
limitations: The skill provides written standards and guidance only. It does not run code or automate any task.
It does not measure token counts or test prompts against a model automatically.
Results depend on the user applying the recommendations to their own prompts.
Guidance is general and may need adjustment for specialized or domain-specific use cases.

use_cases.title: Draft a new agent prompt
use_cases.description: A developer building an AI agent uses the create-prompt workflow to structure a clear system prompt from scratch.

use_cases.title: Trim a bloated prompt
use_cases.description: A prompt engineer applies the optimize-prompt workflow to cut redundant text and sharpen instructions in an existing prompt.

use_cases.title: Standardize team prompt style
use_cases.description: A team lead adopts the standards as a shared reference so everyone writes prompts with consistent structure and clarity.

prompt_templates.title: Basic prompt structure
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me structure a prompt for [task]. Use clear Markdown sections for background, instructions, examples, and constraints.

prompt_templates.title: Make a prompt more direct
prompt_templates.prompt: Rewrite this prompt to use direct, imperative language and remove vague words like might, could, and should: [paste prompt].

prompt_templates.title: Apply just-in-time context loading
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this prompt and replace any large inline data with references that load information only when needed: [paste prompt].
prompt_templates.scenario: Reducing token usage in a data-heavy prompt

prompt_templates.title: Full optimization pass
prompt_templates.prompt: Optimize this prompt using context engineering principles. Remove redundancy, add structure, sharpen language, and show the before and after: [paste prompt].

output_examples.input: Help me structure a prompt for classifying support tickets.
output_examples.output: A structured prompt with four sections: Background describing the ticket domain, Instructions listing the classification steps, Examples showing sample tickets and labels, and Constraints defining the output format.

output_examples.input: Make this prompt more direct: You might want to consider validating the user input before you process it.
output_examples.output: A concise rewrite: Validate user input before processing.

best_practices: Organize every prompt into clear Markdown sections so the model can locate each part of the instruction.
Prefer direct imperative language and remove filler words that add tokens without adding meaning.
Reference large data through identifiers and load details only when the task requires them.
anti_patterns: Dumping full datasets or long histories into the prompt when a short reference would work.
Writing vague instructions with words like might, could, or should instead of clear directives.
Defining several overlapping tools or instructions that duplicate each other and confuse the model.

faq.question: What does this skill do?
faq.answer: It provides standards and workflows for writing clear, well-structured prompts for AI agents such as Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does the skill run any code?
faq.answer: No. The skill contains only Markdown documentation and guidance. It does not execute code or run commands.

faq.question: Who is this skill for?
faq.answer: It is for developers, prompt engineers, and teams who want a consistent, reliable approach to writing prompts.

faq.question: What is context engineering?
faq.answer: It is the practice of selecting the smallest set of high-value tokens that lead the model to the desired outcome.

faq.question: Can it optimize an existing prompt?
faq.answer: Yes. The optimize-prompt workflow guides you to remove redundancy, add structure, and sharpen language in a prompt you already have.

faq.question: What is it based on?
faq.answer: It is based on published Anthropic guidance about effective context engineering for AI agents.
